about: Pune-based company providing robotics, AI, coding and STEM learning solutions to K-12 schools. It sets up educational labs (including Atal Tinkering Labs under tenders and channel partners), supplies learning kits, and sells subscription programmes and other educational services. It also runs a franchise-led activity centre model through a wholly owned subsidiary. Revenue was Rs 93.22 crore in FY26, mostly from lab setup projects.
sector: Education technology / STEM and robotics lab solutions

objects.purpose: Pre-payment or repayment of certain outstanding borrowings

promoters.background: Promoter and Managing Director/Chairman with over 10 years of experience in education, technology-enabled learning and business development. Promoter and promoter group together hold 72.33% pre-issue.

concentration.note: Top 10 customers were 77.99% of FY26 revenue (96.60% in FY24); top customer alone 21.11%, top 3 about 52.6%. Many customers are private firms serving government schools via tenders. Maharashtra was 53.04% of FY26 revenue.

litigation_note: No outstanding criminal, regulatory, material civil or tax proceedings against the company or its subsidiary per the RHP.
strengths: Revenue grew from Rs 38.17 crore in FY24 to Rs 93.22 crore in FY26, about 56% CAGR.
PAT rose to Rs 10.06 crore in FY26 with PAT margin improving from 6.35% to 10.79%.
Reported RoCE of 29.64% and RoNW of 48.66% in FY26.
End-to-end offering: lab setup, kits, curriculum, teacher training and proprietary Drag-on.ai and LMS platforms.
Geographic spread improved: Maharashtra share of revenue fell from 89.86% in FY24 to 53.04% in FY26.
Recurring subscription revenue started, reaching Rs 11.93 crore (12.80% of FY26 revenue).
Debt-equity ratio fell from 3.26 in FY24 to 1.19 in FY26.
No outstanding material litigation, and IPO funds partly repay Rs 2.20 crore of loans.

risks.title: Heavy customer concentration
risks.detail: Top 10 customers made up 77.99% of FY26 revenue (92.95% in FY25, 96.60% in FY24); the largest customer alone was 21.11% and the top 5 were 63.25%.

risks.title: Business is working capital intensive with negative operating cash flow
risks.detail: Net working capital was Rs 31.49 crore in FY26. Operating cash flow was negative in all three years (-Rs 3.64 crore, -Rs 2.10 crore, -Rs 5.10 crore). Receivable days rose to 129 in FY26.

risks.title: Rising debt and reliance on director guarantees
risks.detail: Borrowings doubled to Rs 29.80 crore at Mar-26 (debt-equity 1.19). Some loans carry 16.5% to 18% interest and are secured by personal guarantees of directors.

risks.title: IPO proceeds mostly fund working capital
risks.detail: Rs 23.46 crore of the issue goes to working capital and only Rs 2.20 crore to debt repayment, so the IPO does not fund new capacity. No monitoring agency is required.

risks.title: Regional concentration in Maharashtra
risks.detail: Maharashtra contributed 53.04% of FY26 revenue and 87.28% in FY25; Delhi added 19.99% in FY26.

risks.title: Dependence on schools, institutions and channel partners
risks.detail: Revenue depends on schools, channel partners and tender-based government-linked projects for orders and enrolments, with lumpy lab setup projects at 77.25% of FY26 revenue.

risks.title: Related-party dealings and frequent auditor changes
risks.detail: Transactions with directors and group entities exist (including sales to group entities of Rs 33.75 crore in FY25 and Rs 21.93 crore in FY24 per the related-party table), and statutory auditors changed after resignations.

risks.title: Rapid recent growth with limited peers and valuation reference
risks.detail: FY26 EPS fell to Rs 14.37 from Rs 24.55 after the 3:1 bonus and share issuance; there are no directly comparable listed peers, so valuation is hard to benchmark.

notes: FY26 is Consolidated while FY25 and FY24 are Standalone (subsidiary acquired Mar-26), so growth is not like-for-like. Figures converted from lakhs to crore. Net worth, reserves, EBITDA and ratios are as reported in the KPI table (net worth Rs 20.67 crore excludes capital reserve; balance sheet equity is Rs 25.02 crore). Price band, issue size in rupees, P/E, post-issue holding and GCP amount are blank in the RHP. Borrowings are long plus short term; cash is cash and bank balances. Related-party sales amounts are interpreted from a garbled table and should be treated as approximate. Fresh issue of 29,32,800 shares includes a 1,62,000-share market maker portion; reservation percentages are the SME maximum/minimum allocations (QIB up to 50%, NII 15%, retail at least 35%). Rs 77.20 per share OCD conversion in Sep-26 was reflected in pre-issue shares of 79,26,653.
